purpose: Test whether the AmphiBIO body-size gradient persists when species wet-versus-dry response is first adjusted for pair-level temperature difference, day-of-year difference, rain-contrast magnitude, and year gap.
taxonomy: Reuse exactly the matching rules from NAAMP_RAINFALL_FILTER_TRAIT_CONTRACT_V0_1.json; no new aliases.

primary_model.response: adjusted per-species wet-vs-dry intercept log odds

sensitivities.spearman: unweighted Spearman correlation adjusted log odds vs log body size
sensitivities.family_adjusted: WLS adjusted log odds ~ log body size + C(Family), only if >=18 complete species and residual df >=10
sensitivities.leave_one_family_out: repeat primary WLS after excluding each family represented by >=2 complete species; report all slopes, no threshold rescue

interpretation.negative_primary: Supports a body-size gradient in rainfall-associated active-community filtering that is not explained by pair-level temperature/date differences.
interpretation.family_robust_negative: Strengthens evidence that the gradient is not solely a between-family contrast.
boundary: Body size remains a proxy trait; no direct dehydration physiology has been measured.
No independent-species replication: same NAAMP species response.

prohibited: no removing influential families after seeing slopes
